classification.difficultyReason: Justify equal triangle areas using the midpoint property and a common perpendicular height.

content.prompt:
The midpoint, $M$, of the base of a triangle joins the opposite vertex.
Is the triangle area split in half exactly? Give reasons for your answer.

spec.description: Inverted triangle with a horizontal upper base. Its marked midpoint M joins the lower vertex. Matching double ticks identify the equal base halves. A red dashed vertical height labelled h connects the lower vertex to the upper base. No right-angle marker is supplied.
spec.mathematics: The dividing segment produces two triangles with equal bases and the same perpendicular height.
spec.answerVisibility: The midpoint, ticks, dividing segment and height are permanent givens. No response is shown in the question diagram.

answer.short: Yes. Each triangle has half the original base and the same perpendicular height, so each has half the original area.
answer.worked: The two base segments are equal because $M$ is the midpoint. Both triangles have the same perpendicular height $h$. Since $A=\frac{bh}{2}$, equal bases and equal heights give equal areas, so each triangle has exactly half the original area.
